purpose: Famotidine helps relieve and prevent heartburn, acid indigestion, and upset stomach. It is also used to treat conditions like GERD (acid reflux), stomach ulcers, and esophagitis. Doctors sometimes prescribe it to protect your stomach from excess acid.
how_it_works: Your stomach makes acid with the help of tiny receptors called H2 receptors. Famotidine blocks these receptors, which tells your stomach to produce less acid. With less acid, your heartburn and irritation go away and your stomach and esophagus have a chance to heal.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate famotidine very well. The most common side effects are headache, dizziness, constipation, and diarrhea. Some people may also feel a little nauseous or have stomach discomfort when they first start taking it.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, because your dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid taking it at the same time as antacids unless your doctor says it is okay. If your heartburn or stomach pain does not improve after 2 weeks of using the over-the-counter version, see your doctor. Rarely, some people can have an allergic reaction — stop taking it and seek help right away if you develop rash, swelling, or trouble breathing.
typical_dosing: For over-the-counter heartburn relief, adults typically take 10 mg to 20 mg once or twice a day as needed. For prescription use, doses can range from 20 mg to 40 mg once or twice daily depending on your condition. It can be taken with or without food, and it works best when taken about 15 to 60 minutes before eating or at bedtime.
